messages:
sara: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: remote/hybrid + offsite travel questions. I pulled a few action items and wanted to answer the ones we can now. Please drop any leftover Qs here and we'll update the FAQ. :wave:

alejandro: Thanks — couple quick ones: 1) If my team wants a monthly in-office day, is that set by manager or GMs? 2) Is there any change to the commute reimbursement?

sara: Short answers: managers set team norms (coordinate with your GM for cross-team dependencies). Commute reimbursement remains the same for Colorado/NY pilot locations — any expansion will be announced with 30 days' notice. :thumbsup:

zoe: For the monthly in-office day — do we need to put it on the calendar company-wide or just team calendar?

mike: Team calendar is fine. If it impacts other teams (shared resources, all-hands), loop in the GM. We don't want surprise clashes.

jing: Travel/offsite logistics: please use the new travel request form for bookings and approvals — https://intranet/redwood/travel-requests. The form creates the expense code and routes to finance automatically.

matt: Reimbursements timeline: once expense is submitted, finance target is 10 business days. If you pick a vendor with special billing (e.g., group blocks), ping me and I'll prioritize.

alejandro: For offsites that span international travel, does Redwood cover visa support or letters needed for visas?

jing: Yes — for company-sponsored offsites we provide visa invitation letters and will reimburse visa fees if pre-approved on the travel form. Add a note in the form field "visa support".

sara: A few policy clarifications we promised in the All-Hands Q&A: 1) Hoteling desks remain first-come-first-served unless team books a block. 2) If you need guaranteed desk space for recurring in-office weeks, ask People Ops and we can provision a reserved seat for a quarter.

zoe: Is there any childcare/partner travel stipend for offsites?

mike: We recognize family logistics are real. For 2026 offsites we have a limited childcare stipend pilot — details on the travel page, and managers can request exceptions for team members.

alejandro: Who approves exceptions? e.g., someone needs alternate dates due to family obligations.

sara: Managers + People Ops approve schedule exceptions. If it's about cost we escalate to finance for budget sign-off.

ops-bot: Reminder: submit travel requests at least 21 days before departure to ensure bookings and visa processing when needed. :calendar:

matt: Quick practical: use expense code EXP-OFFSITE-2026 for all offsite travel/room charges. Copy that into your receipts so finance picks it up automatically.

alejandro: Nice, that helps. One policy nuance: can managers require X in-office days per quarter for promotions or is that evaluated separately?

mike: Performance and promotion criteria remain manager-driven but must be documented and equitable. If in-office presence is part of the expectation, it should be stated up-front and consistently applied. People Ops will spot-check for fairness.

jing: Also: if anyone needs ADA-related accommodations (quiet workspace, closer parking, flexible hours), file a request with People Ops and we'll handle confidentially.

sara: Action items I'll own: 1) Update the remote/hybrid FAQ with all answers above by next Tue. 2) Add the childcare stipend pilot details to the travel page. 3) Publish a short checklist for managers to set team in-office norms.

zoe: Thank you! Can you tag the checklist when it's up so we can share with leads?

sara: Will do — I'll post here and in #eng-leads when live.

alejandro: One last tiny ask — is there a preferred vendor list for flights to get group discounts?

matt: Yes — we have negotiated partners. When booking via the travel form, select the vendor dropdown; if it's not listed, pick "other" and tag me.

zoe: :raised_hands: that's great. No more manual invoice headaches.

sara: Thanks everyone. Keep the Qs coming and we'll fold them into the FAQ. If you want private follow-up, DM me or Jing.
